title: Request Limit
brief:
As a shop owner, I want each client limited to a number of requests per minute, so that no single client can overload the shop's server.

Acceptance criteria:
- A client that is over its limit gets 429 with a Retry-After header that says when to try again, and its request is not handled.
- Clients are limited separately: one client over its limit does not slow down another.
- A client gets through again as soon as its earlier accepted requests have dropped out of the last minute, even if it kept retrying in the meantime.

steps.summary: Add the rate limit types and defaults
Add the 429 helper and client identification
Add the check that counts each client's recent requests
Add the request wrapper, unit tests and README docs

probes.question: How many requests per minute does a client get by default?
A request has the headers x-forwarded-for: "10.0.0.1, 10.0.0.2" and x-real-ip: "10.0.0.9". Which client id does it get?
options: unknown

probes.question: A limiter allows 1 request per 1000 ms. A client's request at 0 ms is allowed, and its retry at 300 ms is rejected. Is its next request, at 1200 ms, allowed?
options: Allowed
Rejected
Allowed only after a reset
It throws

items.question: A limiter allows 2 requests per 1000 ms. Requests at 0 ms and 500 ms are allowed. Is a request at exactly 1000 ms allowed?
options: Allowed: the 0 ms request no longer counts
Rejected: the 0 ms request still counts
Allowed only after the limiter has been reset
Checking it throws an error

items.question: A client is over its limit and keeps retrying every 100 ms. When does it get through again?
options: Once its oldest accepted request leaves the window
Only after it has stopped retrying for a full window
On its very next request
Never again, until the server is restarted

items.question: A limiter is created with a limit of 0. What happens when a client sends requests?
options: Only the first request is allowed
Every request is rejected
Every request is allowed: 0 means no limit
Creating the limiter fails as invalid

items.question: Through rateLimited, a client is rejected. It then waits exactly as long as its Retry-After header says, sending nothing in between. Does its next request get through?
options: Yes
No: it is rejected again
Only if no other client sent a request meanwhile
The rejection has no Retry-After header

items.question: Two different clients send requests through rateLimited, neither with any proxy header. Are they limited separately?
options: No: both count as the same client ("unknown")
Yes: each one is limited on its own
Neither of them is limited
rateLimited rejects requests without proxy headers
